definitions.gloss: rime ice on trees; frost-covered trees; ice monsters
definitions.explanation: A natural phenomenon where supercooled water droplets freeze on contact with tree branches, coating them in layers of white ice. Creates dramatic, sculptural formations that are a popular winter tourist attraction in Japan.

examples.japanese: {山頂|さんちょう}で{美|うつく}しい{樹氷|じゅひょう}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: I saw beautiful frost-covered trees at the summit.

examples.japanese: {蔵王|ざおう}の{樹氷|じゅひょう}は{冬|ふゆ}の{名物|めいぶつ}だ。
examples.english: The ice-covered trees of Zao are a famous winter attraction.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{暖冬|だんとう}の{影響|えいきょう}で{樹氷|じゅひょう}の{成長|せいちょう}が{遅|おそ}いらしい。
examples.english: Apparently the rime ice formations are growing slowly this year due to the mild winter.

notes:
A compound of {樹|じゅ} (tree) and {氷|ひょう} (ice). The most famous {樹氷|じゅひょう} in Japan are found at {蔵王|ざおう} in Yamagata Prefecture, where they are nicknamed {樹氷|じゅひょう}モンスター or "snow monsters" (アイスモンスター). They form when strong winds carry supercooled water droplets from the Sea of Japan onto mountain trees.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {樹氷|じゅひょう}を{見|み}に{行|い}く: to go see the frost-covered trees
- {樹氷|じゅひょう}{原|げん}: a field of frost-covered trees
- {樹氷|じゅひょう}ライトアップ: illuminated frost trees (tourist event)

RELATED TERMS:
- {霧氷|むひょう}: rime, frost on trees — a broader meteorological term that includes {樹氷|じゅひょう}
- {氷柱|つらら}: icicle — ice formed by dripping water
- {霜|しも}: frost — ice crystals on the ground or surfaces
